en.title: AMAC Aerospace reports strong demand across maintenance, completions and modifications
en.summary: AMAC Aerospace Group says operations are running at full speed, with Bombardier maintenance projects in Basel up 25% on 2025, a new medevac contract for a Bombardier Challenger, strong demand for Gogo FDX connectivity, and a Boeing Part 145 approval for sister company JCB Aero.
body: Operations are running at full speed at AMAC Aerospace Group of Companies, with new approvals secured, contracts signed and increasing demand across maintenance, completion and modification services. The company says Bombardier maintenance projects at its Basel hangars are up 25% compared with 2025, and it is about to perform its third 8C check on a Bombardier Global Express this year, the first time it has completed three such major inspections on Bombardier aircraft within a single year. It has also signed a new contract for a medevac installation on a Bombardier Challenger aircraft scheduled to arrive at the beginning of 2027, with a possible second project to follow in 2028.

Connectivity installations remain one of its most requested modification services, with particularly strong demand for Gogo FDX, including an ACJ319 currently undergoing installation, a first worldwide installation on a Bombardier Global 5000, and further narrow-body contracts signed for the next three months. Self-defense work also continues to be important: since 2016 the company has equipped nine aircraft with self-defense solutions, completing an installation on an ACJ330 earlier this year with two more Bombardier Challengers in progress. On the completions side, AMAC reports renewed interest in full-scale cabin mockups, which it designs and builds in-house. In August 2026 its sister company JCB Aero, in Auch near Toulouse, received Part 145 Boeing approval covering base and line maintenance on Boeing 737-600, 737-700, 737-800 and 737-900 aircraft, adding to its Airbus Part 145 approval held since MRO services launched in 2024.

zh.title: AMAC Aerospace集團維修、客艙完成與改裝業務需求強勁
zh.summary: AMAC Aerospace集團表示業務全速運轉，巴塞爾的龐巴迪維修專案較2025年增加25%，並簽下龐巴迪挑戰者系列醫療後送改裝合約，Gogo FDX連網改裝需求強勁，姊妹公司JCB Aero也取得波音Part 145認證。
body: AMAC Aerospace集團表示公司業務全速運轉，已取得新的認證、簽署合約，維修、客艙完成與改裝服務的需求持續增加。公司指出，巴塞爾機庫的龐巴迪維修專案較2025年增加25%，今年即將對一架龐巴迪Global Express執行第三次8C檢查，是首度在單一年度內完成三次這類龐巴迪飛機大修檢查。公司也簽下新合約，將為一架預定2027年初交付的龐巴迪挑戰者系列飛機進行醫療後送改裝，並可能在2028年接續第二個專案。

連網改裝仍是需求最強的改裝服務之一，其中Gogo FDX需求尤其強勁，目前有一架ACJ319正在安裝，公司也是全球首家在龐巴迪Global 5000上安裝該系統的業者，未來3個月還有其他窄體機合約已簽署。自衛系統業務同樣重要，自2016年以來公司已為9架飛機裝設自衛解決方案，今年稍早完成一架ACJ330的安裝，另有兩架龐巴迪挑戰者系列飛機正在施工。客艙完成方面，全尺寸客艙模型的需求再度增加，公司可自行設計與建造這類模型。2026年8月，位於土魯斯附近歐什的姊妹公司JCB Aero取得波音Part 145認證，涵蓋B737-600、B737-700、B737-800與B737-900的基地與航線維修，搭配自2024年維修服務啟動以來取得的空中巴士Part 145認證，進一步擴大集團能力。
